bar: Q2 FY27 (Sep quarter) revenue ~$90.9-91.3M and adj EPS $0.55-0.56. Three agreeing sources: MarketBeat 2026-10-19 $90.92M / $0.551 (https://www.marketbeat.com/instant-alerts/upcoming-agilysys-agys-set-to-release-earnings-on-monday-2026-10-19/), Earnings Whispers $91.34M / $0.56, whisper $0.59 (https://beta.earningswhispers.com/go/w/AGYS), Investing.com 2026-10-26 $90.9M / $0.55 (https://in.investing.com/news/stock-market-news/agilysys-earnings-on-deck-can-marriott-rollout-fuel-growth-93CH-5654626). Company guide: FY27 revenue $368-373M, subscription growth >=32%, adj EBITDA 24% of revenue; Q2 subscription growth 'close to 30%' (Q1 FY27 call, https://vectorshift.ai/research/companies/agilysys/earnings/2027-q1). My arithmetic from the guide (subscription +30% on ~$33.4M, maintenance ~$17.5M, product ~$10M, services $19.5-20.4M) gives ~$90.5-91.5M, so the consensus sits on the guided path. Northland's Q2 EPS of $0.37 (July) is an outlier.

findings.finding: Agilysys almost never misses revenue consensus: Q1 FY27 $87.68M vs $85.85M consensus (+2.1%), Q2 FY26 $79.3M vs $76.87M (+3.2%), Q3 FY26 $80.39M vs $79.03M (+1.7%). A similar ~2% beat on this quarter's $90.9-91.3M bar would be ~$92.5-93M, and the company raised its FY revenue guide after each of Q2 FY26 and Q1 FY27.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Revenue beats with a raised guide: +22.6% (Oct 2025), +12.45% (May 2026), +7.23% (Jul 2026). A revenue beat with an EPS miss and weaker subscription implied guide: -19.98% (Jan 2026). The beat by itself does not decide the sign; the EPS line and the guide do.
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced: sell-side estimates were flat over 60 days (Investing.com) while the stock rose 25%, so the price is ahead of the published consensus, which suggests a beat-and-raise buy-side bar above $91M. If the beat were not priced, the stock would not be up twice its group into the print.
findings.independence: Q2 FY26 beat: https://www.tipranks.com/news/the-fly/agilysys-reports-q2-adjusted-eps-40c-consensus-38c-thefly ; Q3 FY26 beat: https://finviz.com/news/287469/agilysys-stock-falls-after-q3-earnings-miss-details ; StockStory says the company 'rarely misses Wall Street's revenue estimates' (https://tradingview.com/news/stockstory:b51f8c4e3094b:0-agilysys-earnings-what-to-look-for-from-agys).

findings.finding: Management guided Q2 FY27 subscription growth to 'close to 30%' (vs 26.1% in Q1), accelerating in Q3 and Q4 to reach the >=32% full-year guide. On reported mix that is ~$43.4M of subscription revenue, a sequential +$3.2M against +$1.5M in the same quarter a year ago. Q1 sales were the best on record, with three seven-figure multi-product wins (two US casino, one Australia), and backlog at a record that excludes the Marriott PMS project.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Subscription growth is the line this stock trades on. Jan 2026 fell -20% when the implied Q4 subscription growth dropped to ~20%. Oct 2025 rose +22.6% on 33.1% subscription growth and a raised subscription guide.
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced: the company guided it in July. What is unpriced is whether Q2 lands above or below 30%. The step-up is double last year's sequential add, so a shortfall to ~27-28% is a real risk on the line that sold the stock in January.
findings.independence: Q1 bookings detail: https://quartr.com/events/agilysys-inc-agys-q1-2027_3POFnXzZ ; Q1 release: https://www.hospitalityupgrade.com/news/agilysys-announces-record-revenue-of-877m-in-fiscal-2027-first-quarter . Both rest on the same Q1 disclosures as the transcript.

findings.finding: Q1 FY27 adj EBITDA was $18.3M, 20.9% of revenue, depressed by a one-time customer conference (CMC preview expected 16-17%). The full-year 24% guide was held, and management expects to exit FY27 near 30%. The guide implies ~25% over the remaining quarters, or ~$22-23M on $91M in Q2, which scales Q1's $0.49 adj EPS to ~$0.58-0.60 against the $0.55-0.56 consensus.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: EPS misses have been punished: Jan 2026 adj EPS $0.42 vs $0.46 consensus with a revenue beat, and the stock fell -20%. Q1 FY27's EPS beat ($0.49 vs $0.40, +26%) bought +7.2%.
findings.why_not_priced: Inside guidance: consensus EPS already +38% YoY prices a margin rebound. The edge is only that my scaling lands slightly above consensus. The whisper ($0.59) is already there.
findings.independence: Q1 transcript on the EBITDA guide and the ~30% exit: https://vectorshift.ai/research/companies/agilysys/earnings/2027-q1 ; whisper $0.59: https://beta.earningswhispers.com/go/w/AGYS

findings.finding: AGYS ran +24.9% in 20 sessions ($96.34 on 09-29 to ~$121 on 10-26) and +8% in 5, against +12.6% for vertical software and +5.3% for IGV. No company news explains it beyond an 8-of-10 AAA casino-list release. Shares sit 14% below the 52-week high and at ~79x trailing earnings, so the buy-side bar for the guide is likely above the published consensus.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Last year's Q2 also came after strength and still rose +22.6% on a raise. Jan 2026 fell -20% from a higher base. No clean history of run-up-conditioned reactions on this name.
findings.why_not_priced: The run-up is the price. The point is that it raises the reaction bar: a routine ~2% beat and a small raise may not hold a 25% advance. If it were not a hurdle, the implied move would sit below the name's own 20% median; it sits at 13.6%, not above it.
findings.independence: Vertical software +12.6% over the month and AGYS +21%: https://tradingview.com/news/stockstory:b51f8c4e3094b:0-agilysys-earnings-what-to-look-for-from-agys ; IGV chart https://query1.finance.yahoo.com/v8/finance/chart/IGV?range=1mo&interval=1d

findings.finding: The Marriott PMS rollout is moving into full-service and premium hotels, with 18-24 months to go, and is excluded from backlog. Management called its revenue assumption 'a pretty conservative estimate of the Marriott rollout', and Oppenheimer says 'more complex Marriott implementations are still ahead'. That is upside to subscription and services if the pace held in Q2.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Marriott contributed only ~0.2pt to FY26 subscription growth. No print has yet turned on a Marriott disclosure.
findings.why_not_priced: Management does not quantify Marriott, so neither consensus nor guide carries an explicit number. The rest of the company (POS high-teens/low-20s growth, flat ~$10M product) has to hold for Marriott upside to show in the total.

lessons_applied: Lesson 1 (a verified fact is not a predicted reaction): beat-history finding cut from +1.0 to +0.8, because this name sold a revenue beat 20% in January when EPS missed.
Lesson 6 (inside the guide): Q2 subscription ~30% and Q1 bookings finding cut from +0.5 to +0.3, and the EBITDA-normalisation finding from +0.6 to +0.3; both are paths the company already guided to.
Lesson 9 (segment net of the rest): Marriott finding cut from +0.5 to +0.4, net of the requirement that POS and product hold.
Lesson 5 (proxy): Hilton RevPAR proxy cut from +0.2 to +0.1; deferred-revenue item cut from -0.2 to -0.1 for lack of a year-ago comparison.
Lesson 7 (positioning): short interest (6.44%, 7.5 DTC) is moderate rather than crowded, so the run-up negative stays at -1.5.
